subject: Proposed fallback + transit safeguards for cross-border processing
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@medicore.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Chu <devops@medicore.com>, Sara Lopez <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on transit safeguards + fallback for EU processing

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Medicore is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Legal and infra have a couple of follow-ups before we can sign the DPA/UK addendum: specifically around cross-border transit safeguards and an operational fallback if the preferred EU model pool is unavailable.

High-level asks:
- A short descriptive flow (diagram or bullets) of how requests that originate from EU patients would be routed and what safeguards (SCCs/UK IDTA reference, TIAs) apply in transit.
- What fallback behavior would we expect if the EU-dedicated capacity is full (e.g., onshore cache, model variant, or routed to US-hosted pool)? What controls/notifications are included?
- Evidence for subprocessor locations and whether you can commit to a monthly subprocessor CSV export.

I attached a spreadsheet with our legal team's clauses and a checklist we use for TIAs. Can someone on your security/privacy side propose language and an operational fallback we can review?

We'd like to avoid a long procurement delay — procurement copied here for cadence.

Best,
Nina
--
Nina Patel | Sr. Counsel, Privacy
Medicore Health
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Evan Chu <devops@medicore.com>, Sara Lopez <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on transit safeguards + fallback for EU processing

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear checklist and the spreadsheet; useful. I pulled together a short operational proposal below and attached a concise evidence bundle we can provide. See inline answers and proposed fallback options.

Summary proposal (high-level):
1) Default routing: EU-origin requests are routed to our EU resident model pool (region: eu-west-1) with SCCs in place and UK IDTA addendum applied for UK-origin data where required. TIAs are scoped per-account; Medicore's TIA will reference dedicated EU model pool + prefix caching technical controls.
2) Fallback tiering (ordered):
   a) Onshore cache: if EU pool is briefly saturated, short-lived prefix/KV cache (edge) returns cached responses for repeated requests where acceptable (TTL < 30s).
   b) EU-compatible quantized variant (same model family, quantized) hosted in eu-west-1 but on lower-priority hosts — slightly higher latency but preserved residency.
   c) Geo-failover to US-dedicated pool (last resort) — route only when the above are exhausted. When this happens: (i) automatic alert to Medicore's security contact, (ii) persistent audit record of routed tokens, (iii) expiration-based residency flagging.
3) Notifications & controls:
   - Real-time webhook + daily digest for any cross-region failovers.
   - Per-route toggle in the Redwood Console for Medicore to opt-in/opt-out of geo-failover.
4) Evidence: enclosed is an evidence-checklist.pdf (architectural diagram + kernel selection log excerpt) and a monthly subprocessor CSV template.

Attachments included: evidence-checklist.pdf, sop_subprocessors.csv.

Next steps: 
- Kimberly, can you help craft the limited contractual language that maps these operational controls to the DPA/UK addendum (TIA language)?
- Jonas, can you confirm the telemetry fields we'll expose (audit logs, token-safe counts, timestamps) and whether onshore cache TTL <30s is supported without additional infra work.

Nina/Sara — if this is acceptable, we can convert the operational parts into a short schedule in the DPA and share a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, EU Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@medicore.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on transit safeguards + fallback for EU processing

Vanessa — drafting comments below (contract-first view). I'll insert these as a short schedule to the DPA and add cross-references to the UK Addendum and TIA. Core points to propose:

- Operationally-limited geo-failover clause: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain EU-resident processing. Geo-failover to non-EU regions shall occur only when (i) EU-dedicated capacity is unavailable AND (ii) no EU-resident cached/quantized variant can serve request. Failover events recorded and retained for 12 months.
- Consent & opt-out control: Medicore has a route-level console control to disable geo-failover. If disabled, Redwood will queue or return 429 when EU capacity saturates.
- Subprocessor CSV commitment: Redwood can provide a monthly CSV export listing subprocessors, region of processing, and a last-reviewed date. We will include a mechanism for notifying Medicore within 10 business days of adding a subprocessor with EU/UK processing footprint.
- Evidence bundle: we'll include a static snapshot (PDF) of recent kernel selection audit logs and a description of caching TTLs.

I recommend we avoid phrasing that promises absolute residency guarantees; instead, use a tiered commitment with notification + auditability.

I'll prepare redline text and share a short snippet for the DPA schedule.

—Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@medicore.com>, Evan Chu <devops@medicore.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on transit safeguards + fallback for EU processing

Quick infra check from my side:
- Onshore cache (edge TTL <30s): supported — we already have ephemeral KV caches in front of the EU pool. I'll add a short note with the cache key scoping (per-tenant prefix) to the evidence PDF.
- Quantized EU-compatible variant: we can provision a lower-priority set; ops estimate ~4 business days to stage and QA.
- Telemetry: we'll expose failover events with these fields: timestamp, request_id (hashed), original_region, routed_region, reason_code. Logs available via S3 export for 90 days and via Console for 30 days.

Operational caveats: if Medicore opts out of geo-failover, request spike patterns may cause increased 429s; we can provide guidance on autoscaling thresholds to reduce that risk.

I'll drop a short appendix to the draft with tech names and retention numbers.

—Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@medicore.com>, Sara Lopez <procurement@medicore.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on transit safeguards + fallback for EU processing

Hi Nina/Sara — pulling this together as an action list and next milestones: 

Action items:
- Vanessa: share DPA schedule draft (includes geo-failover clause, subprocessor CSV commitment, notification timelines) — target 2025-09-05 EOD.
- Kimberly: produce redline language for DPA schedule and short TIA appendix — target 2025-09-05 noon PT.
- Jonas: attach appendix with telemetry fields, retention windows, and cache key scoping into the evidence PDF — target 2025-09-05 EOD.
- Nina: confirm whether Medicore wants geo-failover disabled by default (console toggle) or enabled with notification. If disabled, provide acceptable queueing behavior (prefer queue vs immediate 429).

DocuSign: once Kimberly and Jonas drop their snippets, I'll assemble and send a DocuSign for Medicore's legal/procurement to sign (link will be provided in email).

If helpful, we can do a short (20 min) call Friday to walk the TIA appendix end-to-end.

Thanks all — attaching the evidence-checklist.pdf and a sample sop_subprocessors.csv to this thread for Jessica in procurement to review.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, EU Accounts
Redwood Inference
